text: Lesson one's Slow Request Log told you a transaction took around four seconds, and that most of that time fell under business rules and script execution rather than rendering. That's real progress over a vague complaint, but it still leaves one question open: which script, exactly? This lesson covers the tool built to answer that — script-level debugging, the platform's real script performance profiler.

Say that same incident save fires four scripts: a business rule validating priority, a business rule updating a related problem, the script include method that second rule calls, and a client script setting mandatory fields. A form can easily carry a dozen scripts like these. Without measurement, any of the four could be the two-second bottleneck, and picking which one to investigate first becomes guesswork — maybe you start with whichever name sounds more complicated, or whichever script ran first.

Turn on script debugging and reproduce that exact save, and the guessing stops. The debug panel lists every script that fired, in order, each with its own time: validate priority finishes in a trivial 142 milliseconds, update related problem takes 1894 milliseconds, and a nested line underneath it shows that 1820 of those milliseconds were spent inside one script include method — sync related problems. The client script finishes in 8 milliseconds. Of roughly two seconds total, one method inside one business rule is responsible for the overwhelming majority of it. That's not a hunch. That's a measurement you can act on immediately.

Turning this on takes three real steps. Open the developer menu from your profile picture in the top right and switch on developer mode if it isn't already active. Underneath it, switch on debug business rule and debug script — the two toggles that matter most for this kind of investigation. Then reload the exact page, or repeat the exact save, that was reported as slow, and a debug panel appears at the bottom of the screen listing every script that ran during that one transaction, each stamped with its own elapsed time.

Once you can point to the exact method responsible for a slow transaction, the obvious next question is what inside that method is actually slow — and the most common answer is a GlideRecord query running somewhere it shouldn't. That's lesson six: common GlideRecord performance mistakes, and what one of them looks like once you're watching for it in the profiler.
